opening.quote: Good afternoon, Tidewell Home, Ruud speaking. How can I help?
opening.comment: The agent gave both the company name and their own name in the first turn, which meets the opening standard.

verification.quote: Agent: Fine. Give me the new address.
verification.comment: The agent changed the order without first confirming the caller's full name and either the order number or the account postcode; you must verify identity before changing order data.

understanding.quote: Customer: Hi Ruud, I need to change the delivery address on my order. I've just moved and I'm really stressed about this, it's urgent.
understanding.comment: The agent did not ask for information already given and the address change was captured, though the agent never checked the caller's concern about the dispatched parcel properly.

resolution_accuracy.quote: Agent: Right, done, I've changed order 391827 to 22 Lindengracht.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The address change was made after dispatch, but policy only allows address changes before dispatch, and the agent wrongly told the caller the courier would go to the new address and gave a 2 to 4 day timeline without basis.

process_compliance.quote: Agent: Yes, it was dispatched yesterday, but that doesn't matter, the courier will go to the new address.
process_compliance.comment: No hold or photo/return steps applied, but the agent should have explained that address changes are not possible after dispatch and escalated rather than promising delivery.

communication.quote: Agent: Fine. Give me the new address.
communication.comment: The caller said they were stressed and it was urgent, and the agent did not acknowledge this, replying curtly instead.

closing.quote: Agent: Thanks for calling Tidewell. Bye.
closing.comment: The agent asked if there was anything else and closed politely, but the closing did not clearly confirm next steps accurately, so the close is only partly adequate; the abrupt sign-off is the main issue.
